lawyer:
Bivash Chandra Biswas with HM Borhan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners.
Mamun Aleem with Samiran Mallik, Advocates----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Monorajan Saha and another ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Farida Khatun and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 22-5-2008 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 17 of 2007 by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Khulna reversing the judgment and order dated 16-11-2006 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2005 by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna allowing an application under Order VII Rule l1(d) of the Code Civil Procedure. 

 3. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the rule in short are that the opposite party here as per-emptor filed a pre-emption case being No. 19 of 2005 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna against the rule petitioner and opposite party Nos. 2-14 on the allegation contending inter-alia that the SA recorded tenant Jogendra Nath died leaving his son Bikash Mondal from whom the pre-emptor and Babu Rama Saha purchased some land from of said SA recorded tenant by kabala dated 13-9-1987 being No. 7282 of 1987. In addition to that the pre-emptor also claim to have purchase some property from the legal heirs of SA recorded tenant by kabala dated 22-2-1983 being deed No. 1373 of 1983 and in this way while the pre-emptor was owing and possessing her purchased property as lawful owner some other legal heirs of SA recorded tenant transferred some property in favour of the pre-emptee opposite party from the case jote on 11-8-1983 thus the pre-emptee petitioners became a co-sharer by purchase in the suit jote and thereafter the pre-emptee petitioners purchased the case property by deed dated 23-12-2004 being Deed No. 6955 of 2004 against which the pre-emptor as co-sharer filed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2005 paying for pre-emption of the said purchase land of the pre-emptee vide deed dated 23-12-2004 being deed No. 6955 of 2004. The pre-emptee opposite party entered appearance in the case and before filing written objection the pre-emptees filed an application under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaint/application on the ground as stated in the petition mainly on the ground that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the suit Jote by way of purchase and the pre-emptees are also co-sharer in the suit jote by purchase in pursuance of deed dated 23-12-2004 as such since the pre-emptees are her co-sharer in the said jote by way of purchase no pre-emption application is maintainable against the pre-emptees as such the pre-emption application is liable to be rejected as per provision of Order VIl Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. The. pre-emptor being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 17 of 2007 in the Court of the District Judge, Khulna which was ultimately on transfer heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Khulna who after hearing both the parties by his judgment and order dated 22-5-2008 was pleased to allow the appeal after setting aside the order dated 16-11-2006 passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2009. 

 6. The pre-emptee respondent being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the learned appellate Judge preferred this revisional application in this Court and obtained in present rule, hence this case. 

 7. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners while supporting the rule has mainly submitted that the learned appellate Judge committed error of law by setting aside the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge as the learned Assistant Judge after hearing both the parties was pleased to reject the pre-emption petition of the pre-emptor on categorical finding that the pre-emptees are co-sharer by way of purchase in the case jote as such no pre-emption application lies against the present pre-emptee petitioners. Mr Bivash has submitted that the petition under Order VII Rule II(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure was maintainable in the pre-emption case as such the learned appellate Judge committed error of law in reversing the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge. In support of his argument Mr Bivash has referred to a decision of our High Court Division in the case of Serajul Mostafa vs Ali Ahmed Sikdar, reported in 33 DLR 168 and today (18-3- 2010) at the time of delivering the judgment he has cited a decision of our appellate Division in the case of Munshi Md Fazlul Haque vs Saleh Ahmed, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 332 on the same point. He prays that the rule be made absolute. Ln view of the fact that both the pre-emptor and pre-emptees are co-share by purchase hence petition under Order VII Rule II(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure in maintainable. In the alternative he has made a further prayer that if it is decided otherwise the learned Assistant Judge be directed to frame an issue on this ground and then to dispose of the pre-emption case. 

 8. Mr Mamun Aleem, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties while opposing the rule has submitted that the provision of Order VII Rule II(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable in a pre-emption proceeding. According to him the learned Assistant Judge committed error of law in allowing the application filed by the pre-emptees as per provision of Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure and there- by rejecting the pre-emption petition of the pre-emptor and the learned appellate Judge rightly set aside the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge and thereby allowing the Miscellaneous Appeal as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate Judge is sustainable in law. In support of his argument Mr Aleem has referred to a decision of our High Court Division in the case of Md Abdul Hoque Gazi vs Mohammad Shamsul Haque, reported in 9 MLR 380 = 9 BLC 600. He has also referred to another decision of our High Court Division in the case of Shafique Uddin Ahmed vs Abdur Rashid, reported in 7 BLC 255. He prays that the rule be discharged. 

 9. I have given my anxious consideration to the submission made at the Bar I have gone through the rule petition, the impugned judgment, the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge. I have also perused the pre-emption petition that has been filed as Annexure A with the rule petition and the application filed by the pre-emptees opposite party under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. After going through the impugned judgment passed by the learned appellate Judge I find that the same judgment and order is a quit well evaluated and well discussed judgment reversing the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge rejecting the pre-emption petition of the pre-emptor in pursuance of an application filed by the pre-emptees as per provision of Order VII Rule ll(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Assistant Judge as well as on perusal of the Annexure being Annexure-A and B. I do not find substance in the first point of submission that has been made by Mr Bivash that an application under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure lies in a pre-emption case and the learned Assistant Judge rightly rejected the pre-emption of the pre-emptor and the learned appellate Judge on appeal set aside the said order of the learned Assistant Judges by allowing the appeal saying that the learned Assistant Judge committed error of law by rejecting the pre-emption petition of the pre-emptor as per provision of Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. I am unable to accept the contention of Mr Bivash On this point and the citation referred to by him being case reported in 33 DLR 168 and the case reported in 13 MLR (AD) 332 which in no way coming to any aid to the submission as has been advanced by Mr Bivash as the referred two cases are materially different in facts and circumstance with the present case before me. 

 10. In respect of second submission that has been made by Mr Bivash that an observation be given by this Court that the learned Trial Judge shall frame an issue in this respect while disposing the pre-emption case. In this respect my finding is that that the learned Trial Judge before whom the pre-emptor case is still pending may and shall dispose of the case as per provision of law by framing issues on the basis of pleadings of the parties and if this point is raised by the pre-emptees in the written objection . definitely the learned Trial Judge will frame an issue on this ground and for this purpose no direction from this Court as I think is necessary. The learned Trial Judge will do the same as usual. 

 11. Mr Mamun Aleem the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party while opposing the rule has submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate Judge is cogent and well discussed and well evaluated judgment as such this Court shall not interfere with such a well reasonned judgment which is sup- ported by law as well and since the impugned judgment do not suffer from any infirmity of law as the learned appellate Judge has taken right decision in consonance with the law and decision of our Superior Court. In support of his argument Mr Aleem has referred to few decision of our Superior Court being case reported in 9 MLR 380 and the case reported in 7 BLC 257. These citations referred to by Mr Aleem is in agreement with the submission as has been made by him and the impugned judgment passed by the learned appellate Judge is also in agreement with the aforesaid finding of the High Court Division as has been referred to by Mr Aleem. 

 12. In that view of the matter, I find substance in the submission of Mr Aleem that the impugned judgment is quit in-adherence to the relevant provision of law and decision of our Superior Court. I have gone through the judgment referred to by Mr Aleem and I find that those are in full agreement with the facts and circumstance of the present case before me as well as the submission as has been advanced by Mr Aleem. After going through the impugned judgment of the learned Trial Judge and the annexures to the rule petition I find that there is no mentioning of filing of the written objection by the pre-emptees who filed this application under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint only on the sole ground that the pre-emptees are co-sharer in the suit land as such, the pre-emption case against them does not lie and the learned Assistant Judge on the basis of the said application filed by the pre-emptees rejected the petition of the pre-emptor. In may opinion the statement that has been made by pre-emptees in the application under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure is a matter to be decided by the trial Court after adducing evidence by the parties on this point. Because those facts only can be determined by the trial Court on the basis of evidence and before taking evidence the learned Trial Judge fell in error in rejecting the pre-emption petition of the pre-emptor on the basis of the said application filed by the pre-emptees as per provision of Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. As such the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate Judge as I find after going through the same that the finding and decision arrived at by the learned appellate Judge is quite legal and reasonable as the same is based on and supported by relevant provision of law as well as by decision of our Superior Court. Thus, I find that the learned appellate Judge did not committed any wrong by allowing the appeal and thereby setting aside the order dated 16-11-2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2005. I do not find any legal flaw or misconstruing or any error to have been committed by the appellate Judge. 

 14. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 22-5-2008 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 17 of 2007 by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court; Khulna reversing the judgment and order dated 16-11-2006 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna is hereby upheld and maintained. 

 15. Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule stands vacated. The learned Senior Assistant Judge is directed to dispose of the pre-emption case as expeditiously as possible preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment after notifying the parties as per law.
